name: Parker Solar Probe
first: Closest spacecraft to the Sun ever flown (6.1 M km, 9.86 R☉); first spacecraft to enter the solar corona (2021-04-28); fastest human-made object (192 km/s)
description: Parker Solar Probe ran the highest-energy launch ever flown for a science mission — C3 of 154 km²/s², requiring a custom Star 48BV solid third stage atop a Delta IV Heavy just to escape Earth into a Sun-falling trajectory. Seven Venus gravity assists over six years progressively lowered perihelion from 0.16 AU (P1, 2018-11-05) to 0.046 AU (P22, 2024-12-24 — 9.86 solar radii, 6.1 million km from the surface). At P8 in 2021-04-28 Parker dipped below the Alfvén critical surface — the first spacecraft ever to enter the Sun's corona. At P22 it reached 192 km/s, becoming the fastest human-made object ever. The 11.43-cm carbon-carbon heat shield sustained 1,377 °C while the spacecraft bus 1 metre behind it remained at room temperature.
